title: Parameters A, B, C, D and Graph of y = -(2/pi)*sin(pi*t/2) + 1/pi
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For the general sine function f(t) = A\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{B}(t - C)\right) + D, identify the constants A, B, C, and D for y = -\frac{2}{\pi}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}t\right) + \frac{1}{\pi} and describe its graph.

steps.title: Express the Function in Standard Sinusoid Form
steps.explanation: Write the angular frequency pi/2 as 2*pi/4 and t as t - 0.
steps.why: Matching (2*pi/B)*(t - C) to (pi/2)*t gives 2*pi/B = pi/2, so B = 4 and C = 0.

steps.title: Identify A, B, C, and D
steps.explanation: The coefficient is A = -2/pi (amplitude |A| = 2/pi with vertical reflection), period is B = 4, horizontal shift is C = 0, and vertical shift is D = 1/pi.
steps.why: Direct parameter identification from the standard sinusoid template.

steps.title: Describe the Graph Over One Period [0, 4]
steps.explanation: Because A < 0, the curve initially moves downward from (0, 1/pi) to a minimum of -1/pi at t = 1, crosses the midline y = 1/pi at t = 2, reaches a maximum of 3/pi at t = 3, and returns to 1/pi at t = 4.
steps.why: At t = 1, y = -2/pi + 1/pi = -1/pi; at t = 3, y = 2/pi + 1/pi = 3/pi.
